poems: The vending machine on four takes a dollar and thinks about it.

Nurse Alvarez writes 3:01 in the chart,
then puts her hand back on the woman's ankle.
A gurney parked against a wall, one wheel turned in.

Body temperature bottoms out around now.
Nobody has ever felt impressive at 3:03.
First alarm. Second alarm. Then the baker.

Somebody is being told to wait on the epidural.
Somebody down the hall is being told nothing at all.

For the night float:
round left to right.
Don't wake the man in 12 unless you have to.
Coffee is in the drawer, not the pot.
A moth working the parking lot light like it has a quota.

The ice machine dumps.
Everyone on the floor hears it.
Nobody says anything.
The dog turns twice and lies back down.
The hospice aide keeps her hand exactly where it was an hour ago.

SHELL #4471
PUMP 6 UNLEADED
03:11 AM
CASH
THANK YOU COME AGAIN

You are not going to solve it.
You are going to lie here and rehearse it.
A blood pressure cuff inflating on schedule.
3:14, and nobody awake right now is in the mood for the pi joke.
Quarter past. The refrigerator makes its decision and shuts up.
New father, holding a bottle at the wrong angle, learning it in real time.

Night shift lunch:
Tupperware, microwave, one chair with a wobble.
In Seoul it is late afternoon and someone is bored at a desk.
3:19 a.m. The mind opens a file from 1997 that nobody requested.
A bag of saline, three quarters gone.

The house settles.
It has been settling since 1962 and shows no sign of finishing.

You check the phone. It says 3:22.
It said 3:22 the last time.
Ma'am, I need you to say that one more time for the recording.
Bread proofing in a plastic tub, doubling while nobody supervises.

The fever breaks or it doesn't.
Either way the sheets are ruined.
The cat has opinions about the hallway.
A truck downshifts on the grade two miles off, and you hear the whole thing.

Third shift, n.
The hours a body agrees to work but never agrees to like.

One floor up, someone is being born.
Two floors down, someone is being told.
Same elevator.

The pump alarms because the line kinked, not because anything is wrong,
and it will alarm again.
3:31, and the oven at the bakery has been on for an hour already.
Blue glow under one door down the hall.
3:33. The mind reaches for meaning and comes back holding the number.
Somebody's mother in the chair beside the bed. Upright. Not asleep, not exactly awake.

If it beeps twice, call.
If it beeps once, wait.
If it stops, call.
The pharmacy tech counts to thirty, then counts to thirty again.
An empty lot, lines freshly painted.
3:38 is not a time anyone plans around. It just gets used.
Two people who share a bed, one of them faking it convincingly.
A dog barks four times somewhere east and considers the matter closed.
3:41. The blood draw is scheduled for four, and the arm already knows.

Still open:
the ER,
the truck stop on 29,
the tab you never closed on the laptop.

You will not remember being awake for this.
The body files it under nothing.
Rain on a metal awning, or not.

The chart says no change.
Writing that down takes longer than the change would have.

The night baker's forearms, floured to the elbow,
and this isn't the busy part yet.
An ambulance running without the siren, because there is no one to warn.
3:48. The monitor disagrees with the patient.
By 3:49 the argument you are rehearsing has changed sides twice.
A wheelchair folded against the wall, footrests up.
Somebody in Lagos is eating lunch at a plastic table, out of the wind.
The kettle in the break room has been boiled and abandoned four times tonight.
Milk lets down at 3:53 whether or not anyone was ready for it.
Two moths. One light. No progress.
The security guard walks the loop and finds the same nothing, which is the job.
A woman in a paper gown holds the back of it closed out of habit, not modesty.

Five minutes left of this hour,
and nothing in it has been performed for anybody.

Grease pencil on the whiteboard: BAKE 4:15.
Under it, different handwriting: NO.
3:59. The first alarms of the four o'clock people are already set, across town, in the dark.
